summary: AE + SE reviewed POC success criteria and acceptance tests for ByteHealth pilot. Agreed on go/no-go thresholds: p95 latency < 250ms on hosted/dedicated baseline, inference quality >= 92% on core clinical NER+QA eval set, throughput >= 500 req/min with <0.5% error rate. Reporting will be a daily CSV export and shared dashboard, plus a final slide deck. Redwood to run 48-hour benchmark using ByteHealth sample; security docs to be shared. Next steps and owners assigned.

transcript:
Header: 2025-07-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 56m
Attendees: Sofia Reyes (Redwood AE), Ben Chang (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (ByteHealth CTO), Carlos Ruiz (ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (Security), Liam O'Neill (Product)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Sofia, AE on the account, Ben's our SE who will run the benchmark.
[00:07] Maya: Hi all thanks, we've got a few folks on from ByteHealth. we want to lock success criteria so vendor selection is clear.
[00:13] Ben: yeah hi, Ben here. quick agenda: agree success criteria, confirm workload sample and timeline, and acceptance tests/reporting.
[00:20] Maya: sounds good. high level context: we're building a clinical QA assistant that extracts entities and answers clinician questions, latency matters for UX, but also accuracy is critical. Production target is ~500 concurrent requests/min at peak across multiple regions.
[00:34] Carlos: and just to add, our average prompt length is about 150 tokens, but we have some long context flows - up to 1.2k tokens for patient history.
[00:45] Ben: ok that's helpful. for bench sizing we'll use a 100k token sample that mirrors your distribution - short prompts + the long tails. can you confirm you'll provide that?
[00:55] Carlos: yes, we'll extract an anonymized sample. maybe a couple of notes on PHI redaction - Priya will coordinate.
[01:03] Priya: yep i'll handle redaction and legal signoff. also security requirements: SOC 2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys - we'll need network diagrams for private options.
[01:15] Sofia: great, we'll share SOC2 report and our security deck. regarding KMS we support customer-managed keys for Redwood Private deployments and KMS integration for Dedicated, we'll include the integration notes.
[01:28] Maya: coming to success criteria - we've proposed a few thresholds in the doc you sent. can we walk through them and firm up go/no-go?
[01:36] Ben: sure. first, latency: p95 under normal production mix - goal 250ms for hosted, and for Dedicated we'd expect similar or better depending on instance type. we also propose p50 and p95 reporting.
[01:47] Maya: 250ms p95 is tight given some of our long context requests - how do you handle long context?
[01:53] Ben: we talked about cropping and KV caching. for long patient histories we can cache prefix KV states to reduce repeated compute. note that for 1.2k sequences the cost/latency differs - we'll run separate tests for short vs long flows.
[02:06] Carlos: that makes sense. next, quality: for our NER + QA eval set (approx 2k labeled examples) we need >= 92% F1 for entities and >= 90% exact-match QA score. if model family can't meet that we'd need a fall back or rerank stage.
[02:22] Sofia: ok we'll baseline open models in our catalog and if needed recommend quantized variants or a larger model. acceptance criteria will specify which model variants are allowed.
[02:31] Maya: throughput - target 500 req/min sustained, spikes to 800 req/min for brief periods. error rate needs to be <0.5% across the run.
[02:41] Ben: agreed. we'll include error rate, success rate, and detailed error types in the report (timeouts, 5xx, model OOM).
[02:48] Liam: on reporting - we want a daily CSV export and a dashboard with p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and QA regression alerts. final deliverable: a slide deck with test methodology and raw CSVs.
[03:02] Sofia: that's our standard. we can provide a shared link to a Redwood Console dashboard and also deliver CSVs. the final signoff doc will include the go/no-go decisions per threshold.
[03:11] Maya: what about security posture for hosted vs private? we may prefer Redwood Private for PHI.
[03:16] Priya: yes, ByteHealth's policy is to prefer VPC or Private deployments for PHI. however we can accept hosted if encryption in transit + customer-managed keys and strict retention settings are met.
[03:28] Ben: technically we support both. for the POC we can run benchmarks on a dedicated pool in our hosted environment with strict data retention, or spin up Redwood Private in your VPC for a closer-to-prod test - that will add setup time.
[03:42] Maya: timeline impacts then?
[03:44] Ben: hosted Dedicated pool benchmark can be scheduled within 4 business days of getting the sample. Private deployment takes longer - usually 2-3 weeks for infra and networking.
[03:54] Sofia: for decisioning, do you want the benchmark to represent hosted Dedicated (faster to run) or run Private?
[04:01] Maya: we prefer Private for PHI, but for vendor evaluation maybe hosted Dedicated first to check perf and then a shorter Private validation if needed.
[04:10] Carlos: agreed. so plan: run 48-hour benchmark on Dedicated hosted using the 100k token sample. if results meet thresholds, schedule a short Private validation focused on security and latency.
[04:21] Ben: perfect. acceptance tests - here's what we'll run during the 48-hour window: steady-state run for 24 hours at 500 req/min, two spike tests up to 800 req/min, and long-tail batch tests with the 1.2k token contexts. we'll measure p50/p95, throughput, error rate, and QA metrics against your labeled eval set.
[04:40] Maya: for QA metrics, how will you run the eval? do you run generation and then an automated scorer?
[04:45] Ben: yes we'll run an automated scorer against your labeled examples, compute F1 and exact-match. we'll also run a human spot-check sample of 100 outputs to validate automated scoring - can you allocate someone for that?
[04:56] Maya: yes I can get an ML engineer to spot-check. Carlos will coordinate.
[04:59] Carlos: yep will do.
[05:03] Priya: data residency - we need all data stored in US-only regions and audit logs retained for 1 year; is that configurable?
[05:10] Sofia: yes we support region pinning and audit log retention settings as an add-on. we'll include that in the security doc.
[05:16] Maya: and SSO?
[05:18] Sofia: SAML/SSO is supported; we have RBAC and per-route permissions. we'll share config steps.
[05:25] Maya: ok great. can you write up the final acceptance test matrix?
[05:28] Ben: we'll produce an acceptance matrix that lists each threshold, measurement method, and pass/fail criteria. e.g., Latency: p95 < 250ms measured across 48-hour run with production mix; Quality: NER F1 >= 92% on labeled sample; Throughput: sustained 500 req/min with <0.5% errors.
[05:46] Maya: what's the reporting cadence? daily? and how will you surface regressions?
[05:50] Ben: daily CSVs plus Slack alerts if QA regression > 2% or error rate spikes. final report at end of 48 hours with slides and raw CSVs.
[05:58] Liam: re: cost approx - can you provide an estimate for the 48-hour run and a per-month estimate for dedicated footprint?
[06:05] Sofia: we'll send a pricing ballpark after we know the model variant and allocation. for the POC we can provide a trial credit to cover baseline compute.
[06:14] Maya: ok do we need an NDA update for the sample?
[06:17] Priya: we already have an NDA but i'll confirm it's adequate for sample sharing.
[06:22] Sofia: thanks. any other blockers?
[06:25] Maya: just internal approvals, i'll confirm decision-makers list by Friday.
[06:29] Sofia: perfect. to recap from Redwood side: we'll send final success criteria doc and acceptance matrix, security artifacts (SOC2, KMS notes, region pinning), and benchmark runbook. you'll provide sample data and confirm stakeholders.
[06:44] Maya: sounds good. are these thresholds negotiable? e.g. quality + latency tradeoffs?
[06:48] Ben: yes - the signoff doc can list primary and secondary thresholds; for ex if model hits 90-92% F1 but latency is 20% better, we can list remediation work like rerank or a hybrid pipeline as a conditional pass.
[06:59] Carlos: also want to capture the definition of "error" in the report - e.g., timeouts vs model hallucination.
[07:05] Ben: will include error taxonomy.
[07:08] Sofia: ok, last step - timeline: Redwood to deliver docs by Thu 2025-07-24, ByteHealth to share sample by Fri 2025-07-25, benchmark window 2025-07-28 to 2025-07-29, and final signoff meeting week of 2025-08-04.
[07:26] Maya: confirmed, we'll try to accelerate but that's good.
[07:30] Sofia: thanks everyone - we'll follow up in email with the doc and calendar invites.

End transcript. Note: minor transcription errors may be present (product names sometimes transcribed as Redwood Dedicate or K-V cache).
